Turkey has asked Georgia to launch an inquiry into police violence against Turkish fans during Besiktas’s match against Israeli club Hapoel Be’er-Sheva in Batumi on Thursday night, diplomatic sources told Middle East Eye.
The sources said the Turkish government had demanded action against those responsible. Georgian police moved against Besiktas fans who unfurled a pro-Palestinian banner during the Europa League match.
Turkish officials also summoned the Georgian ambassador to the foreign ministry over the crackdown. The ministry was expected to reprimand the ambassador over footage showing police attacking the fans.
Local police arrested 16 Besiktas fans. Footage of the police intervention sparked public outrage in Turkey and drew condemnation from ministers and opposition leaders.
“The Turkish ambassador in Tbilisi also conveyed our strong protest regarding the police intervention,” a Turkish diplomatic source said.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan called his Georgian counterpart, Maka Botchorishvili, on Thursday night, the source said.
“Officials from the Turkish embassy in Tbilisi and the consulate general in Batumi are at the stadium. All necessary steps are being taken to ensure the safety of our citizens and protect their rights,” the source added.
Besiktas said they had filed an official complaint with European football's governing body Uefa over "disproportionate" use of force by the police.

data.author: Peter Oborne

Teachers arrested, bookshops shuttered, homes demolished, and violent settlers running amok – under occupation, no one is safe from brutal Israeli expansionism
"The first step in liquidating a people is to erase its memory. Destroy its books, its culture, its history. Then have somebody write new books, manufacture a new culture, invent a new history,” wrote the Czech novelist Milan Kundera.
“Before long that nation will begin to forget what it is and what it was. The world around it will forget even faster.”
Kundera’s subject was Czechoslovakia under Soviet communism. His words also apply to life as it is lived in East Jerusalem today under Israeli occupation. An extinguished city where people live abandoned lives of quiet desperation.
For Palestinians, any form of politics has become dangerous. All political activity - campaign meetings, press conferences, canvassing - is banned and punishable by jail.
The governor of Jerusalem appointed by the Palestinian Authority (PA), Adnan Ghaith, once a busy political activist in the Silwan neighbourhood southeast of the Old City, has been arrested 37 times in his seven years in office.
Symbols of national identity are not allowed. Fly a Palestinian flag and you will be arrested. The national anthem is banned. The authorities search schoolchildren's bags, then confiscate books carrying the PA logo. Shopkeepers in the old city are banned from selling T-shirts with Palestinian national symbols.

What if he flew the Israeli flag? “They would send me flowers.”

data.title: Middle East Eye: UK government deleted record of meeting between Blair and Shabana Mahmood
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
UK government deleted record of meeting between Blair and Shabana Mahmood
The British government deleted the record of a meeting between former prime minister Tony Blair and Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, according to the Democracy for Sale newsletter.
The meeting, which took place in June 2025 when Mahmood was justice secretary, was originally declared as official government business, with its purpose listed as "stakeholder engagement".
But when we asked for details of what was discussed under the Freedom of Information Act, the Ministry of Justice told Democracy for Sale it was a "party-political" meeting and that no records of it existed.
Several days after the newsletter asked the government for comment, the meeting disappeared from the public register.
Blair is a member of US President Donald Trump's Gaza "Board of Peace", while Mahmood has pushed for increasingly draconian legislation on migration and maintained the government's ban on Palestine Action.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Pro-Israel groups brand US Gaza advert 'antisemitic Hamas propaganda'
data.author: Oscar Rickett
data.summary:
Pro-Israel groups brand US Gaza advert 'antisemitic Hamas propaganda'
A 30-second advert highlighting US taxpayer funding for Israel was broadcast across the United States on Wednesday night during a Thanksgiving special edition of the long-running sketch show Saturday Night Live.
The ad, from the Institute for Middle East Understanding Policy Project (Imeu), a pro-Palestinian advocacy group based in California, shows an American girl carrying out chores over the course of the year in order to make $400 to buy a new bicycle.
The footage then cuts from the American on a pristine suburban street to a Palestinian girl amid the rubble of Gaza. The Palestinian girl has lost a leg to Israeli bombs and is on crutches.
“Every three seconds, our government sends $400 of taxpayer money to Israel to do this,” says the ad's American narrator, against the backdrop of the girl in Gaza.
The US currently officially gives Israel $3.8bn a year, in a 10-year memorandum of understanding that runs from 2019 to 2028, working out at just over $360 every three seconds.

What will change for Israel, Algeria and Morocco if Spain's right-wing wins elections
“The Israeli government has all our support, affection and understanding,” Santiago Abascal, leader of Spain’s far-right Vox party, said during a trip to Israel in December 2023.
While Abascal visited Israel in a show of support and to seek political backing from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Israeli forces had killed more than 16,248 Palestinians in Gaza, according to figures cited by the UN humanitarian office, OCHA. About 70 percent were women and children.
Spain votes on Sunday, with polls predicting that Vox will almost double its parliamentary representation from 33 seats to 61.
That would help the centre-right People’s Party (PP), which polls project will win 129 seats, assemble a coalition comfortably above the 176-seat majority needed to unseat Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez’s centre-left government.
The election could also change Spain’s foreign policy, including its relationship with US President Donald Trump, its tense relations with Morocco and its deteriorating ties with Israel over the genocide in Gaza and ongoing apartheid policies in the occupied West Bank.

data.title: Middle East Eye: US lobbied Iraq and Venezuela to exit Opec, sparking Saudi intervention
data.author: MEE staff
data.summary:
US lobbied Iraq and Venezuela to exit Opec, sparking Saudi intervention
Submitted by
MEE staff
on
Fri, 11/27/2026 - 15:57
The US pressed Iraq and Venezuela to leave the Saudi-led energy cartel over the summer in a bid to bring down prices
Representatives of Opec member countries attend a press conference after the 45th Joint Ministerial Monitoring Committee and the 33rd Opec and non-Opec Ministerial Meeting in Vienna, Austria, on 5 October 2022 (AFP)
Off
The US tried to break the Saudi Arabian-led energy cartel Opec by lobbying Iraq and Venezuela to leave the organisation earlier this year, sparking a direct intervention from the Saudi Crown Prince, according to a report by Reuters.
The report, published on Friday, reveals how President Donald Trump’s bid to boost production and lower energy prices amid the war on Iran put the US in direct conflict with Saudi Arabia, one of the US's closest allies in the region, which also sells its oil in US dollars and hosts US troops.
The Trump administration’s lobbying over the summer also sheds new light on the decision of the UAE to leave Opec in May.
The Trump administration welcomed the move at the time. Washington extended the option of a currency swap line to the UAE to allow the Emirates to access US dollars if its reserves ran dry. The rare gesture came shortly after the height of fighting between the US and Iran, when oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz had plunged.
Iraq, Saudi Arabia, Venezuela, Iran and Kuwait were the founding members of Opec in 1960.
Iran is already outside the cartel’s purview as a result of US sanctions and its so-called “shadow sale” of oil to China. The withdrawal of Iraq and Venezuela from the alliance would have effectively spelled Opec’s demise, although the alliance has been under pressure for years.

A Palestinian man was killed and several others were wounded on Friday evening in an Israeli drone strike on a vehicle in the northern Gaza Strip, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
The strike hit the vehicle in the Bir al-Naaja area, west of the Jabalia refugee camp, killing Khaled Assaf, witnesses told Wafa.
Some of the wounded were in serious condition.
Separately, a child was wounded by Israeli gunfire in Khan Younis, in the southern Gaza Strip.
Israeli forces stationed near the area's eastern perimeter repeatedly opened fire towards tents sheltering displaced Palestinians, wounding the child.
The Palestinian health ministry said on Thursday that Israeli attacks had killed at least 19 Palestinians and wounded 48 others over the past 48 hours.
The latest attacks brought the total number of Palestinians killed since the so-called ceasefire began in October last year to 1,705.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Gaza's children caught in the grip of a meningitis outbreak
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Gaza's children caught in the grip of a meningitis outbreak
For 10 days, two-month-old Mostafa Hallawin has been bedridden at Al-Rantisi Children’s Hospital in Gaza City. After suffering a persistent high fever, reaching 39C, and recurring abdominal swelling, the Palestinian infant was diagnosed with meningitis.
“It started with a skin rash and a high fever, with his temperature reaching 39C,” his mother, Amal, told Middle East Eye.
“Every day, doctors perform medical scans and laboratory tests,” she added, saying his condition has shown little improvement, largely because of shortages of essential medicines.
Hallawin is one of the most recent children to develop meningitis amid a spike in cases across the war-torn enclave, where Israel has all but destroyed the healthcare system and continues to ban essential medicines.
The UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) reported 413 suspected meningitis cases in Gaza between 27 September and 31 October, including 294 viral and 119 bacterial cases. The report said 68 percent were recorded in Gaza City.
On Tuesday, the Palestinian Health Ministry declared an "epidemic alert" across Gaza, citing a sharp rise in meningitis cases and deaths.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Canada's Supreme Court upholds law banning hijabs in Quebec public sector
data.author: Yasmine El-Sabawi
data.summary:
Canada's Supreme Court upholds law banning hijabs in Quebec public sector
Submitted by
Yasmine El-Sabawi
on
Fri, 11/27/2026 - 16:11
The country's former and only Islamophobia envoy calls the decision "devastating"
A view of the exterior of the Supreme Court of Canada in Ottawa, Ontario, on 12 July 2017 (Creative Commons)
Off
The Supreme Court of Canada on Friday upheld Quebec's highly contested 2019 law that bans religious symbols in the public sector.
It was, more than anything, seen to be targeting Muslim women in the province who wear the hijab, but also impacted Catholics, Sikhs and other minorities.
Quebec's population is 5 percent Muslim, according to the last census carried out in 2021. That figure is second only to Ontario.
Amira Elghawaby, who was Canada’s first and only special representative on combatting Islamophobia, until her office was shut down earlier this year, called the verdict "devastating".
"The promise of Canada’s Charter of Rights and Freedoms has been broken, and could be broken again and again. It means that religious freedoms, equality and the rights of all Canadians are no longer guaranteed," Elghawaby said in a statement released by the organisation she founded this year, the Muslim Communities Research Observatory.
“This ruling will instantly further impact the lives and livelihoods of Quebecers, particularly Muslim women who wear the hijab. In one study, 71% of Muslim women surveyed had considered leaving Quebec, with the province standing to lose an estimated $3.2 billion in income. It may also open the door for further violations of rights and freedoms," she added.
Technicality
Oftentimes rulings by the highest court come down to technicalities.
What the court was looking at in this case was the application of Section 33 of the constitution, known as the "notwithstanding clause", which shields Bill 21 from the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms itself.

Mecca pact members meet in Islamabad and condemn Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
Ministers from Turkey, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan met in Islamabad on Friday to discuss their mutual defence agreement and reiterated their condemnation of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, Pakistan's foreign minister said.
The three countries pledged to intensify efforts to support the kingdom in "safeguarding its security, sovereignty and territorial integrity", Ishaq Dar said in a statement after the meeting.
They also reaffirmed their commitment to more cooperation in defence industries, training and capacity-building, the statement said.
The three countries signed a joint defence agreement in Mecca in August. Recently, countries such as Syria and Indonesia have also expressed interest in joining it.

data.title: Middle East Eye: UN rights chief voices concern as Costa Rica bars Francesca Albanese
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
UN rights chief voices concern as Costa Rica bars Francesca Albanese
Costa Rica denied entry to Francesca Albanese, the United Nations special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territory, drawing criticism from UN human rights chief Volker Turk on Friday.
Turk said he was "deeply concerned" by Costa Rica's decision to bar Albanese from entering the country and urged authorities to reconsider after she was stopped at Juan Santamaria airport, which serves the capital San Jose.
Albanese, an Italian national, had travelled to Costa Rica to receive an honorary doctorate from the state-run University of Costa Rica.
The UN human rights office said on X that Albanese was denied entry on "claimed national security grounds".
The government of Costa Rica asserted that Albanese was the subject of an "international alert over links to terrorist acts".
An Italian lawyer, Albanese is the UN special rapporteur on the situation of human rights in the Palestinian territory, which has been occupied by Israel since 1967. She has been sanctioned by the United States since 2025.
"I am deeply indignant that the government of Costa Rica has spread false information that links me to terrorism," Albanese said from the airport, adding that she hoped Costa Rica would reverse the decision.
Israel's UN ambassador, Danny Danon, praised Costa Rica's decision in a post on X.
Under President Laura Fernandez, Costa Rica has deepened cooperation with the United States on security and moved closer to Israel. It signed a free trade agreement with Israel last year.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Eisenkot says Netanyahu dragging out coalition talks as deadline nears
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Eisenkot says Netanyahu dragging out coalition talks as deadline nears
Gadi Eisenkot, the Israeli opposition leader who is tasked with forming the next Israeli government, said on Friday that Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been dragging out the negotiations, even though his Yashar Party is willing to agree on key points, Haaretz reported.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government, with the possibility of a 14-day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.
According to Haaretz, sources close to Eisenkot's bloc expect Netanyahu to make a significant offer next week to prevent the government Eisenkot is planning from being sworn in.
Yashar and Likud met five times over the past two weeks to negotiate. Eisenkot said that Likud had refused on several days to schedule meetings as frequently as his party proposed.
"Two weeks and five meetings are a sufficient period in which an agreement could already have been reached, if they had wanted one," he said.

data.title: Middle East Eye: Israeli attacks across Gaza kill four Palestinians
data.author: Ayse Betul Aytekin
data.summary:
Israeli attacks across Gaza kill four Palestinians
Israeli attacks killed four Palestinians across the Gaza Strip on Friday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
Several others, including a child, were wounded in a series of attacks across the strip.
In the southern city of Rafah, Gaza's civil defence crews recovered three bodies. They also rescued two wounded people after an Israeli strike near the Muawiya Mosque on al-Bahr Street, in the west of the city.
Wafa reported earlier on Friday that an Israeli drone struck a vehicle in the Bir al-Naaja area, west of the Jabalia refugee camp, killing a Palestinian man and wounding several others, some seriously.
Medical sources and eyewitnesses said Israeli forces stationed near the so-called "Yellow Line" repeatedly opened fire on tents sheltering displaced Palestinians in the area.
The so-called "Yellow Line" is a military boundary imposed by Israeli forces inside the Gaza Strip following the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
Since the ceasefire came into effect in October 2025, more than 1,600 Palestinians have reportedly been killed and 5,833 injured.

Israeli real estate company holds ‘Black Friday’ land sale in Brooklyn
Submitted by

on

Pro-Israel demonstrators threw fire crackers, smoke bombs and eggs at pro-Palestine protesters outside the event
Pro-Palestine protesters gather outside a "Black Friday" event an Israeli real estate company was hosting in Brooklyn, in New York City, promoting the sale of land in Jerusalem on 25 November 2026 (Mounira Elsamra/MEE)
Off
An Israeli real estate group held a "Black Friday" event in Brooklyn on Wednesday, advertising property sales and promoting what activist group Pal-Awda termed "illegal settlement on stolen Palestinian land”.
Firecrackers, smoke bombs and eggs were thrown at protesters by pro-Israel demonstrators outside the real estate event.
Israel's CapitIL real estate agency held the event, selling property in Essen NY Deli in Brooklyn. CapitIL’s website advertises several properties in and around Jerusalem. None publicly advertised is in the occupied West Bank. Middle East Eye was not able to verify which part of Jerusalem the land being promoted was located in. East Jerusalem is occupied according to international law.
Pal-Awda, an organisation that advocates for Palestinian refugees' right of return to their homeland, organised the protest outside the real estate event.
A spokesperson for Pal-Awda called the event "discriminatory" and said they would protest the land sales “no matter where in Palestine the stolen land is located” and that “all of it was taken from dispossessed Palestinians, as part of the ongoing Zionist ethnic cleansing”.
A spokesperson for the group said that these land sales are only open to vetted Jewish Americans who often have no previous or familial ties to Israel, arguing that CapitIL has ties to land sales happening in the occupied West Bank.
